editorial:
Imagine being left all alone in a big house with nothing but your art and your thoughts. That is exactly where you find Anne, a painter who is slowly losing her grip on reality after her husband disappears without a trace. You will feel the tension build as she tries to figure out what happened to him, all while fighting off the dark thoughts in her own head. The vibe is creepy and lonely, making you wonder if she is actually being watched or if she is just imagining things. It is a slow burn that keeps you guessing about what is real and what is just a dream.

What really makes this work is the lead actress who does a great job showing how scared and confused Anne is. The plot twists are surprising, though some parts of the story move a bit slow in the middle. If you like mysteries that mess with your head, you should definitely check this out. For the best experience, try streaming it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video to see all the detail in her paintings, or you can rent it on Apple TV for a quick movie night. It is a solid pick for a rainy weekend.
endingExplained: At the end, you find out that Anne's husband never actually left her. She had a mental break and killed him in a fit of rage, hiding his body in the walls of her studio. The strange things she saw were just her guilt acting up. The movie wraps up with her finally accepting the truth, but she chooses to stay in her lonely house, forever trapped by her own dark secret.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves psychological mysteries and twist endings.
